title: La rivale aux Césars  (The César Rival)

segments.t: At a high-profile photoshoot, Sofia prepares for her turn in front of the cameras. She discovers that Melanie Meyer, who won the Cesar award over her, just finished shooting. Frustrated by constantly feeling second, Sofia shares her doubts with Camille. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Camille, tu peux m'aider un peu?
Bien sûr! Tu es tellement belle aujourd'hui.
C'est enfin mon tour maintenant?
Oui, Mélanie vient de terminer.
Mélanie Meyer? L'actrice du César?
Oui, le Meilleur Espoir Féminin.
Tu le savais déjà, Camille?
Je te jure que non, Sofia.
Elle m'a pris le César!
Je vais toujours arriver deuxième?
Ne pense plus à ce prix.
Tu as un talent immense, Sofia.
Je veux donner le meilleur aujourd'hui.
Montre-leur ta force devant la caméra!
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Camille, tu peux m'aider un peu?
'Camille, can you help me a bit?' Sofia asks her agent for a helping hand with her dress. The modal verb 'can' expresses polite ability in questions.
Bien sûr! Tu es tellement belle aujourd'hui.
'Of course! You are so beautiful today.' Camille warmly praises Sofia's appearance. The intensifier 'tellement' means so or very.
C'est enfin mon tour maintenant?
'Is it finally my turn now?' Sofia wonders if the studio photographer is ready for her. The adverb 'finally' marks relief after a waiting period.
Oui, Mélanie vient de terminer.
'Yes, Melanie has just finished.' Camille lets Sofia know that the preceding session wrapped up. The recent past construction uses 'comes' followed by an infinitive.
Mélanie Meyer? L'actrice du César?
'Melanie Meyer? The actress of the Cesar?' Sofia recognizes the name of the rival actress who won the film prize. The masculine noun 'César film award' refers to the French film academy trophy.
Oui, le Meilleur Espoir Féminin.
'Yes, the Most Promising Actress.' Camille specifies the official category of the award. The adjective 'best' signifies best or foremost.
Tu le savais déjà, Camille?
'Did you already know, Camille?' Sofia asks if her agent had withheld information about the schedule. The direct object pronoun 'it' stands for the situation.
Je te jure que non, Sofia.
'I swear to you no, Sofia.' Camille insists on her complete honesty and innocence. The verb 'swear' means to swear or promise firmly.
Elle m'a pris le César!
'She took the Cesar from me!' Sofia vents her lingering bitterness over losing the trophy. The indirect pronoun 'from me' indicates who was affected by the action.
Je vais toujours arriver deuxième?
'Am I always going to come in second?' Sofia fears that she will constantly remain in the shadow of her rival. The ordinal numeral 'second' means second.
Ne pense plus à ce prix.
'Do not think about that award anymore.' Camille encourages Sofia to focus on the present photoshoot. The negative structure 'not' means no longer or not anymore.
Tu as un talent immense, Sofia.
'You have an immense talent, Sofia.' Camille reminds her of her unique charisma and acting gifts. The adjective 'immense' emphasizes great artistic power.
Je veux donner le meilleur aujourd'hui.
'I want to give the best today.' Sofia finds her determination to shine for the photographer. The expression 'to give' means to do one's very best.
Montre-leur ta force devant la caméra!

'Show them your strength in front of the camera!' Camille gives a final boost of confidence before the flashbulbs fire. The imperative verb 'show' commands bold action on set. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

Sofia overcomes her disappointment and steps onto the photoshoot set with renewed confidence. With Camille cheering her on from the sidelines, she is ready to capture the spotlight. Now let's listen to the scene one last time.
Tu es une grande actrice!
